hook.purpose: Stop the scroll with a specific promise and open a loop that only swiping resolves; doubles as grid thumbnail.
layoutHints: center headline horizontally for grid crop
optional small subline qualifying audience or payoff

intro.purpose: Name the problem, stakes or context so the reader feels addressed; must also work as an entry point if re-served from slide 2.
layoutHints: end on a setup that the next slide pays off

body.purpose: Deliver one point: short headline plus 1-3 supporting sentences.

list.purpose: Several parallel items that belong together, scannable at a glance.

stat.purpose: One striking number with plain-language meaning and a source; works as a pattern interrupt.

quote.purpose: A short memorable line (insight or customer voice) with attribution; adds variety and shareability.

comparison.purpose: Make contrast instantly visible: before/after, wrong/right, myth/fact, old/new.
layoutHints: pair color with icon (x / check), never color alone

step.purpose: One numbered action in a sequence; the number anchors the slide and builds momentum.
layoutHints: large step number in fixed position

summary.purpose: Recap all takeaways on one screenshot-worthy slide; the most save-worthy slide.
layoutHints: mirror wording used in body slides
slightly smaller body allowed but >= minBodyPx

cta.purpose: Ask for exactly one next action tied to the value delivered.
layoutHints: optional secondary ask at lower visual weight

hookTemplates.example: Why does posting daily still get you zero leads?
Your onboarding email is losing you half your trials.
7 spreadsheet formulas that save an hour a week
Stop chasing followers. Build a reply habit instead.
From 3 sales calls to 12 a week: what changed
The one pricing page element most founders forget
How to write a cold email without sounding like a robot
If your team ships late every sprint, read this
The 4-step method for writing headlines that get read

hookRules: be specific (number, outcome, audience or timeframe)
answer lives inside the deck, not on the cover

ctaTemplates.example: Save this for your next product launch.

ctaTemplates.pattern: Send this to a {role} who needs it.
ctaTemplates.example: Send this to a designer who needs it.

ctaTemplates.pattern: Follow for a new {topic} breakdown every {cadence}.
ctaTemplates.example: Follow for a new pricing breakdown every Tuesday.

ctaTemplates.pattern: Which of these do you {verb}? Drop the number below.
ctaTemplates.example: Which of these do you do? Drop the number below.

ctaTemplates.pattern: Comment '{KEYWORD}' and I'll send you the {resource}.
ctaTemplates.example: Comment 'GUIDE' and I'll send you the full template.
Full guide at the link in bio.

ctaTemplates.pattern: Try {first step} today, then tell me how it went.
ctaTemplates.example: Try step 1 today, then tell me how it went.

ctaRules: match CTA type to content type
secondary ask allowed at lower visual weight

swipeCues.where: right edge, hook (optionally all but last)
right edge crossing into next slide

swipeCues.note: setup paid off on next slide

continuity.rule: one N*1080px wide canvas sliced per slide; only decorative elements cross seams; each slide must read alone
one graphic device repeated in a consistent position or role
identical margins, columns and headline baseline across slides
1 background, 1 text, 1-2 accents; each accent has one meaning
page number, handle and progress indicator in fixed positions
vary layout per role within the system; no more than 3 consecutive identical layouts

antiPatterns: more than 50 words on a slide
thin font weight at small sizes
multiple emphasis colors on one slide
critical content within safe inset of edges
stacking many swipe cues on every slide
multiple competing CTAs or no CTA
color as sole carrier of meaning
centered or justified multi-line body text
